title: One-Pot Creamy Chicken and Wild Rice Soup
description: Make this rich, comforting creamy chicken wild rice soup in a single Dutch oven. Minimal cleanup, cozy textures, and ready in under 45 minutes.
story: Weeknight cooking shouldn't mean facing a towering stack of dirty dishes in the sink. This creamy chicken wild rice soup comes together in just one heavy-bottomed Dutch oven, saving you both time and cleanup hassle. During recipe testing, I learned that adding heavy cream while the soup is actively boiling causes it to separate and grain up. Stirring the dairy in off the heat at the very end keeps the broth velvety and smooth. You get tender chicken, earthy wild rice, and aromatic veggies all simmered in one vessel. Are you ready to ditch the extra pots? What is your favorite crusty bread to serve alongside a steaming bowl?
ingredients: 1 cup pre-cooked or parboiled wild rice blend
instructions: Melt the butter in a large Dutch oven over medium heat. Toss in the onion, carrots, and celery, cooking for 6 to 8 minutes until the vegetables soften and the onions turn translucent.
Stir in the minced garlic and cook for about 60 seconds until fragrant, being careful not to let it brown.

Pour in the chicken broth, add the wild rice blend, and submerge the raw chicken breasts right into the liquid. Bring the pot to a gentle boil, then lower the heat to medium-low, cover with a lid, and simmer for 20 minutes until the chicken is cooked through and shreds easily.

Remove the chicken breasts with tongs, shred them on a cutting board using two forks, and return the meat to the pot along with the heavy cream. Stir well off the heat until warmed through and season generously with kosher salt and black pepper before ladling into bowls.
proHack: Use a parboiled or quick-cooking wild rice blend so it fully softens in the same broth cooking time as the chicken breasts without needing a separate pot.
servingIdea: Serve hot with thick slices of warm sourdough bread and a light green salad dressed in a sharp lemon vinaigrette.
storage: Store leftover soup in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. Reheat gently on the stovetop over medium-low heat, adding a splash of chicken broth or milk to thin out the soup as the wild rice continues to absorb liquid.

faqs.question: Can I use leftover rotisserie chicken?
faqs.answer: Yes. Skip simmering raw chicken in the broth and simply stir in 2 cups of shredded rotisserie chicken during the last 5 minutes of cooking to warm it through.

faqs.question: How do I prevent the rice from getting mushy?
faqs.answer: Make sure you use a standard wild rice blend rather than instant white rice, and turn off the heat immediately after adding the cream so the starches don't over-thicken.
